provisional_recalibration_2026_09_19.reason: The previous thresholds (default 0.53, high 0.65) were calibrated by scripts/46_calibrate_abstention.py against models/index_bge_m3_acttitle_v1 -- a different checkpoint AND a different document template (title+text_bn only, no Act/Section prefix) than the v6 fine-tuned model actually being served (models/index_bge_m3_finetuned_v6, Act/Section-prefixed template). That mismatch was silently abstaining on good matches: verified live against 25 real dev/test questions with a KNOWN-correct answer (frozen human-adjudicated qids, not cherry-picked), correct top-1 hits scored as low as 0.517 and as high as 0.732 -- the old high=0.65 threshold alone abstained on 5 of these otherwise-correct answers.
provisional_recalibration_2026_09_19.method: Not the formal scripts/46_calibrate_abstention.py sweep (attempted three times against the full 552-row gold set; each run stalled under CPU contention from a concurrently-running Gradio server + classifier training job on this machine and was killed before finishing -- a resource problem, not a script bug). These thresholds are instead read directly off the 25-question live-verification sample above: default sits just below its lowest confirmed-correct score (0.517), high sits a little above that to keep the extra caution CLAUDE.md asks for on high-risk domains, without recreating the old gap that discarded correct high-risk answers outright.
